Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-dfd447f7: Count sparse markers per panel

When the grid has full divider rows/columns (color may vary) separating equal-sized panels, treat each panel as one output cell. Count the sparse marker cells in each panel, ignoring divider lines. In demonstrated instances, the marker color has varied (8 in an earlier example, 0 in the accepted 19×19 case), so identify markers as the sparse non-field color rather than assuming the marker is always 8. Output one cell per panel: use the panel-field/background color where a panel contains zero or one marker, and use color 1 where a panel contains more than one marker. Discard divider rows/columns and preserve panel layout.

## Evidence / validated recurrence

- Demo: 11×11 grid, color-0 full divider rows 3 and 7 and columns 3 and 7. This creates a 3×3 matrix of 3×3 panels. Each panel has one 8 except the bottom-right panel, which has two (at local positions (1,1) and (2,2)). Output is 3×3, background color 5, with only bottom-right set to 1.
- Prior test: 19×11 grid, color-2 full divider rows 4, 9, 14 and columns 3, 7. This creates a 4×3 matrix of 4×3 panels. Two panels in panel-row 2 (zero-indexed), columns 0 and 2, each contain two 8s; all other panels contain at most one. Accepted output is 4×3, background color 0, with 1s at (2,0) and (2,2), all other cells 0.
- Accepted recurrence: 19×19 grid, divider color 9 at rows/columns 4, 9, 14, forming sixteen 4×4 panels. Field color is 5; sparse markers are 0. Marker counts by panel were [[2,2,2,1],[2,2,2,2],[1,2,2,2],[2,2,2,1]]. Accepted 4×4 output uses 1 for counts >1 and 5 for counts 0 or 1: [[1,1,1,5],[1,1,1,1],[5,1,1,1],[1,1,1,5]].
